q: Does organic carbon in limestone add to a cement plant's CBAM figure?
title: Organic carbon in raw meal and CBAM
short: Yes. Carbon in the raw meal that is not carbonate, such as organic matter or shale carbon, burns off in the kiln and the resulting CO2 counts as a process emission. It is usually small next to calcination, but it belongs in the figure when you report actual emissions.
audience: Cement plant process and environment teams preparing CBAM data

p: Some limestone, clay and shale carry organic carbon. In the preheater it oxidises to CO2 alongside calcination CO2.

ul: Test total organic carbon in raw meal as part of your lab routine.
Multiply carbon content by raw meal tonnes and by 44/12 to get CO2.
Report it with calcination as a process emission.

p: If tests show it is negligible, record the tests and the reason in your monitoring notes rather than leaving it out silently.
